register.name: 2-year Treasury note (GDN170228), Regional Government Securities Market
register.detail: Government of Grenada · auction of 16 February 2026 · rate 5.50% · 17 bids worth EC$15.5M · due 17 February 2028
register.note: Bids of EC$15.5 million for an issue of EC$10 million
register.text: A two-year Treasury note of EC$10 million, sold by auction on the Regional Government Securities Market of the Eastern Caribbean at 5.50 percent, the cap set in the 2026 prospectus. It is the first issue of the 2026 programme, which refinances maturing securities in Eastern Caribbean dollars.

register.name: Treasury bill and note programme, Regional Government Securities Market, 2026
register.detail: Government of Grenada · prospectus for issues from January to December 2026 · eight auctions of 91-day and 365-day Treasury bills and one 2-year Treasury note · rate caps of 3.50% to 5.50%
register.note: In 2025 eight auctions on the market raised EC$144.3 million (Ministry of Finance, Debt Report 2025)
register.text: The Government’s programme of issues on the Regional Government Securities Market for 2026: EC$150 million in Treasury bills and a Treasury note. The issues refinance maturing securities and lower the cost of borrowing by reducing reliance on the overdraft facility.

register.name: Restructured international bonds due 2030: natural disaster clause invoked after Hurricane Beryl
register.detail: Government of Grenada · payments due November 2024 and May 2025 deferred · added to the lump-sum payments due at maturity in 2030 · IMF staff report, January 2026
register.note: The first time such a clause has been invoked, according to the IMF; 0.9% of 2024 GDP
register.text: After Hurricane Beryl in 2024, Grenada deferred two near-term payments on its restructured international commercial bonds under a disaster clause, the first time such a clause has been invoked, according to the IMF. The deferred US$12 million is added to the payments due at maturity in 2030, which left cash for recovery; the Ministry of Finance states that the deferred payments will be honoured in line with the revised terms.

register.name: Climate Actions for Building Resilience in Coastal Communities (CABRIC) in the Caribbean, FP325
register.detail: Green Climate Fund · approved by the Board on 28 October 2026 (B.46) · grant · accredited entity: Caribbean Community Climate Change Centre · the Bahamas, Belize, Grenada, Jamaica and Saint Lucia
register.note: A grant for five nations; the share for Grenada is not stated; about 983,000 people expected to gain resilience
register.text: A Green Climate Fund grant of US$42.04 million, with US$2.0 million of in-kind co-financing, for a facility of small, medium and large grants for locally led adaptation in five Caribbean nations, Grenada among them. It finances climate-resilient agriculture, ecosystem-based fisheries, mangrove restoration, last-mile early warning, and resilient shelters and clinics, serving the food, shelter, health and livelihood standards.

register.name: Caribbean Resilient Renewable Energy Infrastructure Investment Facility (RREIIF)
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · approved 17 April 2025 · P180831 · Grenada, Saint Lucia, and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines · Ministry of Finance release of 10 July 2025
register.note: Grenada’s share, from its IDA20 concessional allocation; the regional facility is of US$110 million
register.text: A regional World Bank facility of US$110 million that pools renewable energy projects across three nations to lower costs and attract private developers, modernises transmission and distribution with battery storage, and uses partial credit guarantees to mobilise up to US$120 million of commercial credit. Grenada’s part is US$20 million of IDA concessional financing; it serves the energy standard.

register.name: Caribbean Efficient and Green Energy Buildings Project
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) and Clean Technology Fund · approved 28 February 2025 · P179519 · IDA US$40M and a CTF loan of US$8.5M · 40-year maturity with 10 years’ grace (Ministry of Finance)
register.note: Grenada’s part of a US$131.87 million project for Grenada, Guyana and Saint Lucia
register.text: IDA concessional financing of US$40 million and a Clean Technology Fund loan of US$8.5 million to reduce energy use in public buildings in Grenada and increase the adoption of renewable energy systems. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: CCRIF parametric insurance payouts after Hurricane Beryl
register.detail: CCRIF SPC · tropical cyclone, excess rainfall and COAST (fisheries) policies of the Government · handed over in July 2024 · paid within 14 days of the event · EC$118M
register.note: US$55.6 million in all to CCRIF members in Grenada, including the electricity and water utilities
register.text: Parametric insurance payouts of more than US$44 million (EC$118 million) to the Government of Grenada under its tropical cyclone, excess rainfall and fisheries policies, after Hurricane Beryl. CCRIF pays within 14 days of an event, which gave the Government early cash for relief and recovery.

register.name: Disaster Risk Management Development Policy Credit with a Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · approved 21 January 2020 · P171465 · drawable on an official declaration of emergency within three years, renewable for three more · used after Hurricane Beryl in 2024 (IMF)
register.note: The first Cat DDO approved for the region under IDA
register.text: A US$20 million IDA credit that gives Grenada contingent financing for disasters and health emergencies, drawable on an official declaration of emergency, with reforms for disaster resilience in schools and climate criteria in public investment. The IMF reports that Grenada used this Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option after Hurricane Beryl in 2024.

register.name: Second Recovery and Resilience Programmatic DPC
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · approved 20 July 2023 · closed 31 December 2024 · fully disbursed · series outcome rated Satisfactory (IEG)
register.text: Budget support tied to recovery and resilience reforms, the second of a two-credit series. Both credits were fully disbursed as scheduled, and the series closed on 31 December 2024 with an outcome rated Satisfactory by the World Bank’s Independent Evaluation Group.
register.note: The second of two credits, US$25 million in 2022 and US$30 million in 2023, US$55 million in all

register.name: Enhanced direct access pilot for adaptation and community resilience, FP061
register.detail: Green Climate Fund · accredited entity: Department of Environment, Antigua and Barbuda · Antigua and Barbuda, Dominica and Grenada · closing date 16 December 2026 · annual report for 2025, July 2026
register.note: Grenada’s committed share of US$20 million; US$2.76 million disbursed to Grenada to the end of 2025
register.text: Green Climate Fund financing of US$20 million for three Eastern Caribbean nations, of which US$6.31 million is committed to Grenada, executed by the Ministry of Climate Resilience. In Grenada it has rehabilitated the Programme for Adolescent Mothers facility, with rainwater harvesting, and finances a Climate Adaptation Revolving Loan Fund at the Grenada Development Bank, more than 97% disbursed, with 54% of beneficiaries female-headed households.

register.name: Geothermal Drilling Project – Grenada
register.detail: Caribbean Development Bank · approved in 2023 · two exploratory wells · test drilling under way in March 2025, to be followed by production drilling
register.note: Enhanced from 2025 under CDB’s GeoSmart Initiative with UK funds
register.text: CDB financing of US$9.4 million, approved in 2023, for geothermal drilling in Grenada, including two exploratory wells. Geothermal power is a local, renewable source of electricity, and the project serves the energy standard.

register.name: Geothermal test drilling: memorandum of understanding with the United Kingdom
register.detail: UK FCDO, Caribbean Development Bank and Government of Grenada · news release of 24 March 2025 · under CDB’s GeoSmart Initiative
register.note: To enhance the Geothermal Drilling Project; test drilling to be followed by production drilling
register.text: A £10 million memorandum of understanding between the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office, the Caribbean Development Bank and the Government of Grenada to support geothermal test drilling in Grenada. It adds to the CDB’s US$9.4 million drilling project and serves the energy standard.

items.name: Grenada Chocolate Company
items.text: A small cooperative of cocoa farmers and chocolate makers that grows cocoa to organic standards on more than 80 hectares and makes its own bars in Grenada, set up so that small farmers are paid fairly and share in its profits.
